issues.description: play.ts is a scratch debugging file committed into the diff
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from a local relative path and contains console.log experiments about metadata ordering. This is hammock-time scratch work that should not ship in a PR. It complects 'I was thinking about this' with 'this is the change'. Remove it or move it to a test that asserts behavior instead of printing it.

issues.description: flattenRef now complects three different inheritance/dedup concerns in one function
issues.detail: finalize/flattenRef now handles: processor-ref inheritance, parent-chain refinement subtraction, $ref-extraction dedup, and a second parent-was-extracted $ref propagation pass. Four distinct concerns are intertwined behind shared mutation of `schema`, ordering-dependent `seen.ref = null` guards, and JSON.stringify equality. This is the textbook complecting the lens exists to name; each concern wants its own pass over values, not braided mutation.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as structural equality is incidental complexity hiding a real question
issues.detail: Dedup compares `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. Key order, undefined fields, and nested object identity all silently change behavior. The essential question is 'does the child redundantly restate a parent fact'; encoding that as string equality is the easy answer, not the simple one. A small structural-equality helper on plain values would say what is meant.

issues.description: Seen.ref overloaded with three meanings: unset, null-as-sentinel, and 'inherit from'
issues.detail: `ref?: $ZodType | null` is used as (a) processor-provided inheritance source, (b) parent fallback when unset, and (c) null sentinel meaning 'already flattened, do not recurse'. Three distinct states on one field. Splitting into `inheritFrom` (value) and `flattened` (boolean) would make the time semantics of the traversal explicit instead of encoded in mutation order.

issues.description: Override count doubled from 6 to 12 with no explanation of why that is correct
issues.detail: The test assertion changed from `toBe(6)` to `toBe(12)`. The previous code explicitly skipped overrides on `isParent`; the new code removed that skip. Doubling override invocations is a real behavior change for users with custom overrides and deserves either a code comment explaining why parent overrides are now correct, or a separate test pinning the new semantics on purpose.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked: what is a 'parent' as a value?
issues.detail: The fix threads a new `parent` field, repurposes `ref`, adds a propagation pass, and changes file-processor output shape. Before more keyboard time, name the value model: a schema has an inheritance edge (processor-declared) and a clone edge (structural parent); JSON Schema output is a function of those edges plus extracted-defs identity. Once those are values, most of the mutation in flattenRef disappears.

review.summary: The change fixes a real bug in metadata propagation across wrapped schemas, but it does so by adding a second inheritance edge (`parent`) on top of the existing `ref` and braiding four concerns — processor inheritance, parent-chain refinement, extracted-def dedup, and parent-$ref propagation — into one mutating finalize pass. This is COMPLECTED and EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: the diff is small because the team knows this code, not because the design got simpler. Structural equality via JSON.stringify and tri-state `ref` are INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY the values model could remove. The committed play.ts scratch file and an unexplained 6→12 override count change should not ship as-is.
